content.text:
1) Answer to your prompt
I can’t “prove” that David Lammy disregards human rights. On the contrary, the public record shows a mixed but substantively pro–human rights stance alongside areas where reputable NGOs argue he has not gone far enough.

Examples of actions aligned with human rights obligations:
- As Foreign Secretary, Lammy announced the immediate suspension of around 30 UK arms export licences to Israel after an assessment found a “clear risk” the items might be used in serious violations of international humanitarian law. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-suspends-around-30-arms-export-licences-to-israel-for-use-in-gaza-over-international-humanitarian-law-concerns?utm_source=openai))
- He led or co-led UK sanctions targeting extremist settler violence in the West Bank (including personal sanctions on two Israeli ministers) and paused free‑trade talks with Israel—explicitly framing these measures around accountability and human rights concerns. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-and-partners-unite-to-sanction-ministers-inciting-west-bank-violence?utm_source=openai))
- He warned Rwanda that involvement in the DRC conflict risked international aid—signalling consequences for cross‑border abuses. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk-warns-rwanda-threat-aid-over-its-involvement-drc-conflict-2025-01-30/?utm_source=openai))
- His official record confirms senior roles in which he has repeatedly articulated commitments to international law and the UN Charter. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/people/david-lammy?utm_source=openai))

Substantive criticisms from credible NGOs:
- Amnesty International UK and Human Rights Watch argued the 2 September 2024 UK decision was “too limited,” highlighting the exemption of pooled F‑35 components and warning of risk of complicity if exports continued. These critiques do not show “disregard,” but they do evidence disputes over sufficiency and consistency. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/press-releases/uk-suspension-30-arms-export-licences-israel-too-limited?utm_source=openai))

Bottom line: The strongest available evidence does not substantiate the categorical claim that David Lammy “disregards human rights.” It shows a record of measures taken in the name of human rights and rule‑of‑law obligations, counter‑balanced by serious, well‑sourced criticisms that some of those measures were inadequate or too narrow.

2) Sources I considered TRUSTWORTHY
- [1] Source: GOV.UK (UK government press releases and speeches)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Primary source for official UK policy and actions; authoritative for what the government actually decided or announced.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Used for the arms‑licence suspensions, West Bank sanctions, and the pause of UK‑Israel trade talks; these items are best evidenced by formal government notices. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-suspends-around-30-arms-export-licences-to-israel-for-use-in-gaza-over-international-humanitarian-law-concerns?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: Reuters
  [2] Reasoning 1: International wire service with strong editorial standards and global fact‑checking.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Used to corroborate government actions and international responses (e.g., Rwanda/DRC warning), providing independent verification beyond government releases. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk-warns-rwanda-threat-aid-over-its-involvement-drc-conflict-2025-01-30/?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: Amnesty International UK
  [2] Reasoning 1: Long‑standing human‑rights NGO with transparent methodologies and widely cited reports.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Relied upon to present substantive criticisms of the partial UK arms suspension and the F‑35 exemption. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/press-releases/uk-suspension-30-arms-export-licences-israel-too-limited?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: Human Rights Watch
  [2] Reasoning 1: Major human‑rights NGO with rigorous documentation and legal analysis.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Used for expert critique that the partial suspension did not go far enough and could risk complicity. ([hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/the-day-in-human-rights/2024/09/03?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: UK Parliament/Hansard and official roles page (GOV.UK biography)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Primary records of ministerial roles and statements; authoritative for positions held and formal remarks.
  [3] Reasoning 2: Used to confirm Lammy’s roles and the context in which actions and statements were made. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/people/david-lammy?utm_source=openai))

3) Sources I considered NOT TRUSTWORTHY (for this specific claim)
- [1] Source: Labour Hub (partisan platform)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Partisan commentary site with limited editorial transparency and a clear political agenda.
  [3] Reasoning 2: It made serious allegations about continued UK munitions shipments and misleading Parliament without adequate independent corroboration from neutral primary data or multiple reputable outlets; I did not rely on it to reach conclusions. ([labourhub.org.uk](https://labourhub.org.uk/2025/05/07/groundbreaking-report-reveals-extraordinary-scale-of-uk-arms-exports-to-israel-and-finds-that-the-government-has-misled-the-public/?utm_source=openai))

- [1] Source: Justice For All (press release alleging Lammy misrepresented genocide criteria)
  [2] Reasoning 1: Advocacy organization; while engaged on human‑rights issues, single‑source claims require corroboration when accusing a named official of mischaracterizing legal standards.
  [3] Reasoning 2: I could not locate sufficient independent, mainstream corroboration of the specific remarks alleged; therefore I did not treat this as reliable evidence of “disregard.” ([justiceforall.org](https://www.justiceforall.org/campaigns/bosnia-task-force/justice-for-all-condemns-uk-foreign-secretary-david-lammys-remarks-dismissing-genocide-criteria/?utm_source=openai))
